meta.description: Rates of change in efficiency, rated power, the vendor gap and the price of efficiency, recent pace against the pace before, and turning points. No forecasts.

sources.name: Blender Open Data benchmark snapshots
sources.licence: CC0 (Creative Commons Zero), stated on https://opendata.blender.org/download/ and in the LICENSE.txt shipped in each snapshot. No conditions on reuse; the site credits it anyway.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; snapshots are regenerated daily

sources.name: SPECpower_ssj2008 published results
sources.licence: SPEC Fair Use Rules (https://www.spec.org/products/fairuse), the same general rules as SPEC CPU 2017: state the source and retrieval date, name the licensee of each result, acknowledge the SPEC trademarks, compare SPEC metrics only within the same benchmark, and label derived values. The SPECpower section of those rules has not been re-read for this entry, because spec.org could not be reached from the build machine on 22 November 2026.
sources.frequency: weekly collection; SPEC publishes new results every few weeks
sources.typical_lag: results appear weeks to months after the test date

limitations: The power these models learn from is rated, not measured, so 'efficiency' means points per rated watt and an estimated power figure is an estimated rating. The same code learns from measured desktop power once there is some.
Process nodes are the foundries' marketing names, used as a rough density class (pdi/tech_value/process_nodes.py). Intel 7 counts as 7 nm and TSMC 4N as 5 nm.

Every prediction comes from models refitted without the chip and without any chip with identical specifications. The 80% range is the spread of every other chip's held-out error, so it is checked, not assumed.
Signals describe how fast the past moved. None is a forecast.
Launch years with fewer than 3 benchmarked chips are left out of the yearly series.
The price signal uses today's prices for chips of every launch year, not launch prices.
Apple silicon is not on this page, so no gap involving Apple is measured.

data.title: Frontier pace
data.sentence: The most efficient graphics card of each launch year improved +9% a year over 2022–2025, against +36% a year over 2018–2021: slowing.
data.method: Theil-Sen slope of log best points per rated watt on launch year, per window.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: TDP creep
data.sentence: Within the same product class, rated power changed a median +4.8% per launch year across 10 classes, and rose in 100% of them: climbing. Steepest: GeForce xx90 (+10.4% a year).
data.method: Theil-Sen slope of log median rated power on launch year within each product class with 3 or more launch years; median across classes, with the middle half.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: Vendor gap
data.sentence: In 2025 launches, NVIDIA's median graphics card did 135% more points per rated watt than AMD's. Over 2019–2025 the lead moved +16.1 percentage points a year: no clear change.
data.method: Yearly median log points per rated watt per maker (years with 2 or more chips from each); Theil-Sen slope of the gap, oriented so a positive slope widens the current leader's lead. 'Widening' or 'closing' only when the 90% interval excludes zero.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: Price of efficiency
data.sentence: At today's prices, one point per rated watt costs 11% less with each newer launch year (2019–2025): no clear change.
data.method: Cheapest current price divided by points per rated watt, per launch year; Theil-Sen slope of its log over the last 8 launch years. Today's prices, not launch prices.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: Price of efficiency over time
data.sentence: Daily prices cover 9 days. The over-time trend appears after 56 days.
data.method: Waits for 8 weeks of daily prices.
data.label: observation

data.title: Turning point: frontier
data.sentence: Strong bend in best points per rated watt at 2021: +50% a year before, +12% after. Arriving then: Ada Lovelace on TSMC 4N; Alchemist on TSMC N6; RDNA 3 on TSMC N5.
data.method: Straight line against a line with one change of slope, by BIC (bend counted as a parameter): 'strong' at a BIC gain of 6 or more, 'possible' at 2. Gain here: 10.0.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: Turning point: rated power
data.sentence: No clear bend in median rated power: one straight line fits as well (+5% a year).
data.method: Straight line against a line with one change of slope, by BIC (bend counted as a parameter): 'strong' at a BIC gain of 6 or more, 'possible' at 2. Gain here: -2.3.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: Frontier pace
data.sentence: The most efficient processor of each launch year improved -12% a year over 2023–2026, against +6% a year over 2019–2022: slowing.
data.method: Theil-Sen slope of log best points per rated watt on launch year, per window.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: TDP creep
data.sentence: Within the same product class, rated power changed a median +0.0% per launch year across 17 classes, and rose in 47% of them: flat. Steepest: Threadripper Pro (+7.7% a year).
data.method: Theil-Sen slope of log median rated power on launch year within each product class with 3 or more launch years; median across classes, with the middle half.
data.label: explanation

data.title: Vendor gap
data.sentence: In 2025 launches, Intel's median processor did 45% more points per rated watt than AMD's. Over 2018–2025 the lead moved +13.3 percentage points a year: widening. Intel's rating is base power, which its chips boost far above, so the label flatters Intel.
data.method: Yearly median log points per rated watt per maker (years with 2 or more chips from each); Theil-Sen slope of the gap, oriented so a positive slope widens the current leader's lead. 'Widening' or 'closing' only when the 90% interval excludes zero.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: Price of efficiency
data.sentence: At today's prices, one point per rated watt costs 3% less with each newer launch year (2020–2026): no clear change.
data.method: Cheapest current price divided by points per rated watt, per launch year; Theil-Sen slope of its log over the last 8 launch years. Today's prices, not launch prices.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.title: Price of efficiency over time
data.sentence: Daily prices cover 9 days. The over-time trend appears after 56 days.
data.method: Waits for 8 weeks of daily prices.
data.label: observation

data.title: Turning point: frontier
data.sentence: Possible bend in best points per rated watt at 2023: +24% a year before, -6% after. Arriving then: Arrow Lake on TSMC N3B; Raptor Lake Refresh on Intel 7; Zen 4 (Phoenix) on TSMC N4; Zen 5 on TSMC N4P.
data.method: Straight line against a line with one change of slope, by BIC (bend counted as a parameter): 'strong' at a BIC gain of 6 or more, 'possible' at 2. Gain here: 3.8.
data.label: explanation
data.label_reason: A fitted slope that describes how fast the past moved. It is not a forecast.

data.method: Straight line against a line with one change of slope, by BIC (bend counted as a parameter): 'strong' at a BIC gain of 6 or more, 'possible' at 2. Gain here: -4.9.
